meta.content: Adding pydantic parsing to a Hydra app
meta.name: description

admonition.title: tl;dr
admonition.paragraph: When wrapping your main function with hydra_zen.zen, pass in hydra_zen.third_party.pydantic.pydantic_parser to the instantiation_wrapper argument of zen. Additionally, for any hydra_zen.instantiate calls you make, pass this parser in as the _target_wrapper_ argument.

admonition.title: Prerequisites
admonition.paragraph: Your must install pydantic in your Python environment in order to complete this How-To guide.

section.names: add\ pydantic\ type\ checking\ and\ parsing\ to\ your\ hydra\ app pydantic-parsing
section.title: Add Pydantic Type Checking and Parsing to Your Hydra App
section.paragraph: Hydra’s runtime type checking is limited to only a narrow subset of Python’s typing features. By contrast, Pydantic provides much more comprehensive type checking capabilities; additionally, it is capable of parsing CLI inputs into complex data structures (e.g., convert a string to a pathlib.Path). In this how-to guide, we will add pydantic parsing to all config-instantiation sites in our Hydra-app.
Consider the following simple hydra-zen app:

container.caption: Contents of my_app.py
container.literal_block:
from hydra_zen import store from hydra_zen.third_party.pydantic import pydantic_parser
from typing import Literal from pydantic import PositiveInt
from dataclasses import dataclass
@dataclass class Character: age: PositiveInt = 22 name: str = "Bobby"
def main( character: Character, gear: tuple[str, ...] = (), mode: Literal["easy", "hard"] = "easy", ): print(f"{character=!r} {gear=!r} {mode=!r}")
if __name__ == "__main__": from hydra_zen import zen
store(main, hydra_defaults=["_self_", {"character": "base"}]) store(Character, group="character", name="base") store.add_to_hydra_store()
zen( main, # This is the key ingredient instantiation_wrapper=pydantic_parser, ).hydra_main( config_name="main", config_path=None, version_base="1.3", )

section.paragraph: By specifying instantiation_wrapper=pydantic_parser in our hydra_zen.zen call, we insure that all config-instantiation sites in our Hydra-app will use pydantic parsing. Because of this, we will benefit from the following features:

list_item.paragraph: Annotating mode with Literal will restrict the permitted values for this parameter.
We can configure gear with a list of strings at the CLI and - because of the tuple[str, ...] annotation - it will be coerced into a tuple of strings before being passed to main.
We can use a pydantic.PositiveInt annotation for the character.age nested field; this will ensure that the age is a valid value.

section.paragraph: Let’s check that mode is restricted to the values easy and hard:

container.caption: Running the app with an invalid value for mode
container.literal_block: $ python my_app.py mode='medium' Traceback (most recent call last): ... pydantic_core._pydantic_core.ValidationError: 1 validation error for main mode Input should be 'easy' or 'hard'

section.paragraph: Next, let’s see that gear can be passed a list, which will be coerced into a tuple:

container.caption: Running the app with a list of strings for gear
container.literal_block: $ python my_app.py gear='[sword,shield]' character=Character(age=22, name='Bobby') gear=('sword', 'shield') mode='easy'

section.paragraph: Finally, let’s see that character.age is correctly parsed as a PositiveInt:

container.caption: Running the app with an invalid value for character.age
container.literal_block: $ python my_app.py character.age=-1 Traceback (most recent call last): ... Error in call to target '__main__.Character': 1 validation error for Character age Input should be greater than 0

section.paragraph: In this way, we can use Pydantic to add powerful type checking and parsing to our Hydra apps.

If your app includes manual calls to hydra_zen.instantiate, you can also pass in the pydantic_parser as the _target_wrapper_ argument to ensure that these config-instantiation calls also use Pydantic parsing.

note.paragraph: Keep in mind that this pydantic parsing layer only occurs when we instantiate configs that have _target_ fields, and that it uses the annotations of the _target_ objects.
